items.title: 14.1.7 Distance Between Two Points in Space (Roman Urdu)

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 14.1.8 chhaapti hai (Book# 14.1.8). Kitab mein 14.1.1 naam ki koi heading hai hi nahin, is liye portal 14.1 ke sub-headings ko tarteeb se 14.1.1 se 14.1.8 tak number karta hai. Yahan 14.1.7 wahi hai jo kitab mein 14.1.8 hai.

Ab ek bohat kaam ki cheez: space mein do points ke darmiyan faasla. Ghar se school ka faasla, ya ek jahaz se doosre jahaz ka faasla, sab isi formula se nikalta hai. Achhi baat yeh hai ke humein koi nayi cheez yaad nahin karni: pehle do points ke beech ka vector banayenge (14.1.3 ka \"aakhri minus shuru\"), phir us ki magnitude lenge (14.1.4 ka formula). Bas!

Agar \(\overrightarrow{OP_{1}}\) aur \(\overrightarrow{OP_{2}}\) points \(P_{1}(x_{1}, y_{1}, z_{1})\) aur \(P_{2}(x_{2}, y_{2}, z_{2})\) ke position vectors hon, to vector \(\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}}\) yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: vector P1P2 equals OP2 minus OP1
equals x2 minus x1, y2 minus y1, z2 minus z1
distance equals magnitude of P1P2 equals square root of x2 minus x1 squared plus y2 minus y1 squared plus z2 minus z1 squared

blocks.alt: Axes x, y, z from O. Arrows from O go to the points P1(x1, y1, z1) and P2(x2, y2, z2), labelled OP1 and OP2. A third arrow goes from P1 to P2, labelled P1P2.
blocks.caption: Position vectors OP1, OP2 and the vector P1P2 = OP2 − OP1 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ise \(R^{3}\) mein do points \(P_{1}\) aur \(P_{2}\) ke darmiyan distance formula kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: \(\overrightarrow{OP_{2}} - \overrightarrow{OP_{1}}\) kyun? Figure dekhiye: \(O\) se \(P_{1}\) jaana aur phir \(P_{1}\) se \(P_{2}\) jaana, seedha \(O\) se \(P_{2}\) jaane ke barabar hai: \(\overrightarrow{OP_{1}} + \overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}} = \overrightarrow{OP_{2}}\). Dono taraf se \(\overrightarrow{OP_{1}}\) hata dein to formula mil jaata hai.
Distance formula asal mein 14.1.4 wala magnitude formula hai jo \(\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}}\) par lagaya gaya. Har farq ka square hota hai, aur \((x_{2} - x_{1})^{2} = (x_{1} - x_{2})^{2}\), is liye points ki tarteeb badalne se faasla nahin badalta.
Plane wale formula \(\sqrt{(x_{2} - x_{1})^{2} + (y_{2} - y_{1})^{2}}\) mein bas ek square aur jur gaya hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice.) \(A(1, 0, 1)\) aur \(B(4, 4, 7)\) ka faasla.
\(\underline{AB} = [4 - 1,\ 4 - 0,\ 7 - 1] = [3, 4, 6]\)
\(|\underline{AB}| = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 36} = \sqrt{61} \approx 7.81\)
Tasdeeq: ulti tarteeb se \([-3, -4, -6]\), squares phir bhi \(9 + 16 + 36 = 61\).

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Suppose a butterfly's flight path passed through points \((2, 4, 7)\) and \((6, 1, 3)\), where each unit represents a meter. What is the magnitude of the displacement the butterfly experienced in traveling between these two points?
steps:
Given: \(P_{1}(2, 4, 7)\), \(P_{2}(6, 1, 3)\); 1 unit = 1 meter.
To find: \(P_{1}\) se \(P_{2}\) tak displacement ki magnitude.
Method: sab se pehle samajhte hain ke displacement kya hai: shuru ke point se aakhri point tak ka seedha vector \(\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}}\). Us ki magnitude do points ka faasla hai, is liye distance formula lagega. Titli ka asal raasta tedha meda ho sakta hai, lekin displacement sirf seedhi line dekhta hai.

Distance formula likhein
\[d = \sqrt{(x_{2} - x_{1})^{2} + (y_{2} - y_{1})^{2} + (z_{2} - z_{1})^{2}}\]
Kyun: yeh \(|\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}}|\) hai, yani displacement vector ki lambai.

Farq nikaalein (displacement vector)
\[\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}} = [6 - 2,\ 1 - 4,\ 3 - 7]\]
\[= [4, -3, -4]\]
Kyun: aakhri point minus shuru ka point, har component alag. Titli x mein 4 m aage gayi, y mein 3 m peeche aur z mein 4 m neeche aayi.

Formula mein rakh kar hal karein
\[d = \sqrt{(6 - 2)^{2} + (1 - 4)^{2} + (3 - 7)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{16 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{41}\]
\[\approx 6.40\]
Kyun: \((-3)^{2} = 9\) aur \((-4)^{2} = 16\); square kabhi negative nahin hota. \(\sqrt{41} \approx 6.403\), do decimal tak 6.40.

Tasdeeq: faasle ke liye points ki tarteeb se farq nahin parta.
\[\sqrt{(2 - 6)^{2} + (4 - 1)^{2} + (7 - 3)^{2}} = \sqrt{16 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{41}\]
Aur \(6.40^{2} = 40.96 \approx 41\). Sahi!

blocks.text: Is misaal se ek ahem farq yaad rakhiye: distance (faasla) scalar hai aur displacement vector. Titli ka displacement vector \([4, -3, -4]\) hai, jo simt bhi batata hai; us ki magnitude \(\sqrt{41}\) m sirf yeh batati hai ke shuru aur aakhri jagah kitni door hain. Agar titli ne raaste mein chakkar lagaye hon to us ka kul safar (path length) is se ziyada hoga, lekin displacement wahi rahega.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(P(5, -2, 4)\) aur \(Q(2, 2, 4)\) ka faasla kitna hai? Dekhiye z-coordinates barabar hain.
Jawab: \(\sqrt{(2 - 5)^{2} + (2 + 2)^{2} + 0^{2}} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\). Jab ek coordinate barabar ho to us ka farq sifar aata hai aur sawal plane jaisa ban jaata hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
\(\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}} = \overrightarrow{OP_{2}} - \overrightarrow{OP_{1}} = [x_{2} - x_{1},\ y_{2} - y_{1},\ z_{2} - z_{1}]\).
Faasla \(= |\overrightarrow{P_{1}P_{2}}|\): teen farq, un ke squares, jama, phir square root.
Displacement ki magnitude seedhi line ka faasla hai, raasta jaisa bhi ho.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Coordinates minus karne ki jagah jama kar dena: \(x_{2} - x_{1}\) chahiye, \(x_{2} + x_{1}\) nahin.
Negative number ko minus karte waqt sign ki ghalti: \(2 - (-2) = 4\).
\(-3\) ka square \(-9\) likh dena; sahi \(9\) hai.
Word problem mein unit (yahan metre) likhna bhool jaana.
